page: Microsoft Azure E8-4ds_v6 is an Edsv6-family virtual machine configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16 GB per vCPU. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions. The virtual machine is managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and includes 472 GB of local storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2170.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 31.35 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics show some limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is registered at 3990.17, and the multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed is 26.15 GB/sec, both falling into the lower performance tiers. Large-block memory read bandwidth is measured at 37.14 GB/sec, while write bandwidth is 25.89 GB/sec. For database operations, the instance achieves a PassMark database score of 2890.86 and handles 5.71 million Redis SET operations per second.

Given the high memory density relative to compute resources, the E8-4ds_v6 is structured for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel CPU scaling. The inclusion of 472 GB of local storage and Premium Storage capability makes it suitable for relational databases, caching layers, and memory-bound data processing. While single-threaded execution is highly efficient, the lower multi-core scaling and moderate memory bandwidth suggest it is less optimal for heavy multi-threaded compilation or large-scale LLM inference, where text generation for a 7B model reaches only 4.5 tokens per second.
